items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer introduces Chester Campbell, Sr. as the father of Mr. Chester Campbell, Jr., who is providing the information. The interviewee (Maxine Sullivan) is not present during this introduction and does not speak about her personal relationship with Chester Campbell, Sr.

ctx.x: the 22nd of July, I'm back at the house that jazz built and we're about to start the third interview session with Maxine Sullivan. She stepped out of the room right now and while she's away I thought I might get something interesting on the tape here. I was lucky to run into Mr. Chester Campbell, Jr., and he's going to talk a little bit about his father.
My dad, Chester Campbell, Sr., was born in Cumberland, Maryland. He was an orphan and the man that raised him taught him to play the E-flat tuba.

He went on the road with a show called, In Old Kentucky when he was a youngster and in 1926 he brought his bride, Eleanor Campbell and his four youngsters to New York. He played with Cliff Jackson, he played a stint with Earl Hines, he played a stint with Cab Calloway. He switched to the string bass around the early 30s and he took lessons from a German fella for $2.00 a lesson in the front room of our home.
